stem: A wound culture has been ordered for a wound with clinical signs of infection. Which swab-collection technique best supports an interpretable specimen?

options.A: Cleanse the wound, select viable wound-bed tissue, and rotate the swab over about 1 cm² with enough pressure to express wound fluid while avoiding pus, slough, eschar, necrotic material, and surface exudate.
options.B: Collect drainage from the surrounding skin before cleansing because surface exudate best represents organisms in viable wound tissue.
options.C: Swab necrotic tissue preferentially because devitalized material provides the most accurate sample of the organisms driving invasive infection.
options.D: Skip wound-bed assessment and culture every chronic wound routinely because bacterial growth on a swab confirms that the wound is infected.

rationale: A is correct. Current NCBI nursing guidance for wound-culture collection directs the nurse to irrigate and cleanse the wound to remove surface debris, identify approximately 1 cm² of viable tissue, and rotate the swab over that area with sufficient pressure to express wound fluid. The specimen should not be taken from pus, slough, eschar, necrotic tissue, or skin exudate. B and C increase the chance of sampling surface colonizers or nonviable material rather than the clinically relevant wound bed. D is incorrect because wound cultures are obtained when infection is suspected and bacterial presence on a chronic wound does not by itself establish clinical infection. Tissue sampling may be preferred when deeper or more definitive microbiologic assessment is needed.
educational_objective: When a wound swab culture is indicated, obtain the specimen from cleansed viable wound-bed tissue using pressure to express tissue fluid and avoid superficial exudate or necrotic material so the result better represents clinically relevant organisms.
source_organization: National Library of Medicine / NCBI Bookshelf
source_document_title: Nursing Skills — Chapter 20 Wound Care, 20.9 Checklist for Wound Culture
source_version_date: Current NCBI Bookshelf nursing text accessed 2026-08-17
source_locator: Section 20.9 Checklist for Wound Culture, steps 9–20: irrigate with sterile normal saline to remove surface debris/exudate; wipe surface contaminants; identify a 1-cm² area of viable wound tissue; do not sample pus, slough, eschar, or necrotic tissue; rotate swab over the selected area for 5 seconds with sufficient pressure to express wound fluid; never collect exudate from the skin.
source_claim_supported: For an indicated wound swab culture, cleansing followed by pressure swabbing of viable wound-bed tissue yields a more clinically appropriate specimen than superficial exudate or necrotic material; the culture result must still be interpreted in clinical context.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing
blueprint_locator: Physiological Integrity — Reduction of Risk Potential: obtain diagnostic specimens correctly, monitor for infection-related complications, and use laboratory results to reduce risk.
blueprint_topic: Reduction of Risk Potential — wound culture specimen quality
correction_summary: Rebuilt the raw Levine-technique rationale into a specimen-quality decision and corrected the blueprint from Basic Care and Comfort to Reduction of Risk Potential. The final item avoids claiming that swab culture universally outperforms tissue biopsy and instead tests the directly supported collection steps and limitations.
audit_reviewer: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol — Rule 1 clinical audit + adversarial second pass

audit_findings.source_audit: Verified against NCBI Nursing Skills 20.9 and corroborated with current wound-management evidence that Levine-style swabbing is an acceptable practical method when a swab is indicated, while tissue sampling may be more definitive in selected wounds.
audit_findings.claim_by_claim: A reproduces the source-supported wound cleansing, viable-tissue selection, pressure, and avoidance of surface/necrotic material. B and C sample less clinically useful material. D confuses colonization with clinical infection and promotes indiscriminate culture.
audit_findings.choice_A: Correct; evidence-based swab collection from cleansed viable tissue.
audit_findings.choice_B: Incorrect; surface drainage can reflect colonizers and contamination.
audit_findings.choice_C: Incorrect; necrotic material is specifically excluded from the recommended specimen site.
audit_findings.choice_D: Incorrect; wound culture is not a stand-alone test for whether a chronic wound is clinically infected.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: The item asks for the best swab technique when a swab culture has already been ordered, avoiding the separate question of when tissue biopsy is preferred. Only A follows the complete collection method.
audit_findings.cueing: All options address wound-culture collection or interpretation rather than unrelated wound care.
audit_findings.blueprint: Diagnostic specimen quality and infection-risk reduction fit Reduction of Risk Potential.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Rechecked swab-versus-tissue evidence, chronic-wound colonization, wound cleansing, viable-tissue selection, and numeric 1-cm²/5-second technique. The final answer does not overclaim swab superiority and no second defensible answer remained.
